summary: Four rules are switched off for this repository, and only these four.
Everything else was fixed in the code: 6.23 -> 9.20 through real refactoring.
Each exemption is a case where the rule is wrong for this shape of code, not a
case of the code being wrong. See README, 'Scoring itself'.
(Rule names cannot be commented inline: an unrecognised name inside `rules` is
a hard error, deliberately, so that a typo can never silently disable a rule.)
Number of Functions in a Single Module: metrics.rs is 54 measurement primitives and detectors.rs is 34 (19 rules plus
helpers). Both are catalogues: every item is small, named, and belongs beside
its neighbours. Splitting them into sub-modules to satisfy a count would
scatter cohesive code and help nobody.
It is also in direct tension with Bumpy Road and Large Method, which is what
settled it: extracting function_name into three named helpers fixed its Bumpy
Road finding and pushed the module from 52 functions to 54. Past that point you
are trading one finding for another rather than improving anything.
Lines of Code in a Single File: Same three files, same argument. 568 lines of measurement primitives is a
readable module; five files of 110 lines each, split on no principle, is not.
Low Cohesion: Fires on Profile and GateReport, a config object and a report struct. Their
predicates each consult a different field by design, so LCOM4 reads three
accessors of three lists as three unrelated jobs. This is the known LCOM4 blind
spot for data objects, already documented under Known limitations.
Constructors, pure accessors and associated functions are already excluded from
the metric; these are what is left.
Primitive Obsession: Fires on gate_side(label, score, detail) and on difflib's matches_before and
matches_after, which take four byte indices because that is what a search
window is. In Rust, usize indices and &str labels are the vocabulary of small
